plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Sturdy stems carry daisy-like blooms with rosy-pink petals that sweep back from a spiky, copper-orange central cone. The flowers draw butterflies, bumblebees and goldfinches all through the heat of high summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August (peak mid to late summer)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies, meadows and native gardens
plants.funFact: The prickly central cone is made of hundreds of tiny fertile florets. The genus name comes from the Greek word for hedgehog, 'echinos'.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling fields of silvery-green foliage turn violet-blue when slender flower spikes open and release a sweet, herbal perfume. Bees hum through the rows, and the scent drifts for miles on warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with true lavender peaking from late June to mid-July and the hybrid lavandin peaking in mid to late July
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and Mediterranean-climate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a crown of silky, pointed bracts around a fuzzy heart. It blooms in the cool, wet South African winter, when much of the northern world is in full summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring (June to October)
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa, including the slopes around Cape Town
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. It is adapted to fire-prone fynbos and survives bushfires thanks to its thick underground stems.
